with the given method and data.\n\n        Args:\n            url (str): The URL to which the request is sent.\n            method (str): The HTTP method to use (\'GET\', \'POST\', \'PUT\', etc.). Check for SQL Injection vulnerabilities\n        if self.detect_sql_injection(response[\'body\']):\n            vulnerabilities.append({\n                \'type\': \'SQL Injection\',\n                \'description\': \'SQL injection vulnerability detected.\',\n                \'payload\': response[\'body\']\n            })\n\n        # Check for XSS vulnerabilities\n        if self.detect_xss(response[\'body\']):\n            vulnerabilities.append({\n                \'type\': \'XSS\',\n                \'description\': \'Cross-site scripting vulnerability detected.\',\n                \'payload\': response[\'body\']\n            })\n\n        # Check for CSRF vulnerabilities\n        if self.detect_csrf(response[\'headers\']):\n            vulnerabilities.append({\n                \'type\': \'CSRF\',\n                \'description\': \'Cross-site request forgery vulnerability detected.\',\n                \'payload\': response[\'headers\']\n            })\n\n        return vulnerabilities\n\n    def detect_sql_injection(self, content: str) -> bool:\n        """\n        Detects potential SQL injection vectors in a given content string.\n\n        Args:\n            content (str): The content to scan for SQL injection patterns.\n\n        Returns:\n            bool: True if potential SQL injection patterns are found, False otherwise.\n        """\n        sql_injection_patterns = [\'\\\' OR 1=1\', \'admin\\\'--\', \'DROP TABLE\']\n        return any(pattern in content for pattern in sql_injection_patterns)\n\n    def detect_xss(self, content: str) -> bool:\n        """\n        Detects potential XSS (Cross-site Scripting) vectors in a given content string.\n\n        Args:\n            content (str): The content to scan for XSS patterns.\n\n        Returns:\n            bool: True if potential XSS patterns are found, False otherwise.\n        """\n        xss_patterns = [\'<script>\', \'javascript:\', \'<iframe\', \'onerror=\']\n        return any(pattern in content for pattern in xss_patterns)\n\n    def detect_csrf(self, headers: dict) -> bool:\n        """\n        Detects potential CSRF (Cross-site Request Forgery) vulnerabilities based on headers.\n\n        Args:\n            headers (dict): The HTTP headers to check for CSRF vulnerabilities.\n\n        Returns:\n            bool: True if headers lack CSRF protections, False otherwise.\n        """\n        # Typically, CSRF protections involve checking for specific tokens in headers\n        return \'X-CSRF-Token\' not in headers and \'SameSite\' not in headers\n\n```\n\n\n\n# Format example 1\n## Code Review: vulnerability_scanner.py\n1. POST, PUT, DELETE, and HEAD.\n    """\n    \n    def send_request(self, url: str, method: str = \'GET\', data: dict = None) -> dict:\n        """\n        Send an HTTP request to the specified URL with the given method and data.\n\n        Args:\n            url (str): The URL to which the request is sent.\n            method (str): The HTTP method to use (\'GET\', \'POST\', \'PUT\', etc.). Default is \'GET\'.\n            data (dict): The data to be sent in the request for methods like POST and PUT. Default is None.\n\n        Returns:\n            dict: A dictionary representing the response received from the server.\n        """\n        try:\n            # Parse the URL to extract components\n            parsed_url = urlparse(url)\n            host = parsed_url.netloc\n            path = parsed_url.path\n            if parsed_url.query:\n                path += \'?\' + parsed_url.query\n\n            # Create a connection based on the scheme\n            if parsed_url.scheme == "https":\n                conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection(host)\n            else:\n                conn = http.client.HTTPConnection(host)\n\n            # Prepare headers and body\n            headers = {\n                \'Content-type\': \'application/x-www-form-urlencoded\',\n                \'Accept\': \'text/plain\'\n            }\n            body = None\n            if data and method in [\'POST\', \'PUT\', \'DELETE\']:\n                body = urlencode(data)\n                headers[\'Content-Length\'] = str(len(body))\n\n            # Send the request\n            conn.request(method, path, body, headers)\n            response = conn.getresponse()\n\n            # Read and return the response\n            response_data = response.read()\n            conn.close()\n\n            return {\n                \'status\': response.status,\n                \'reason\': response.reason,\n                \'headers\': response.getheaders(),\n                \'body\': response_data.decode()\n            }\n        except Exception as e:\n            return {\'status\': \'error\', \'reason\': str(e)}\n```\n----- vulnerability_scanner.py\n```import re\n\nclass VulnerabilityScanner:\n    """\n    This class scans HTTP responses for potential vulnerabilities.\n    It is designed to identify common security issues such as SQL injection, XSS, and CSRF.\n    """\n\n    def scan_for_vulnerabilities(self, response: dict) -> list:\n        """\n        Scans the given HTTP response for vulnerabilities.\n\n        Args:\n            response (dict): The HTTP response dictionary containing status, headers, and body.\n\n        Returns:\n            list: A list of dictionaries, each representing a found vulnerability.\n        """\n        vulnerabilities = []\n        # urllib.parse import urlparse, urlencode\n\nclass HttpRequests:\n    """\n    This class handles HTTP interactions by sending requests to specified URLs.\n    It supports various HTTP methods like GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, and HEAD.\n    """\n    \n    def send_request(self, url: str, method: str = \'GET\', data: dict = None) -> dict:\n        """\n        Send an HTTP request to the specified URL with the given method and data.\n\n        Args:\n            url (str): The URL to which the request is sent.\n            method (str): The HTTP method to use (\'GET\', \'POST\', \'PUT\', etc.). Default is \'GET\'.\n            data (dict): The data to be sent in the request for methods like POST and PUT. Default is None.\n\n        Returns:\n            dict: A dictionary representing the response received from the server.\n        """\n        try:\n            # Parse the URL to extract components\n            parsed_url = urlparse(url)\n            host = parsed_url.netloc\n            path = parsed_url.path\n            if parsed_url.query:\n                path += \'?\' + parsed_url.query\n\n            # Create a connection based on the scheme\n            if parsed_url.scheme == "https":\n                conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection(host)\n            else:\n                conn = http.client.HTTPConnection(host)\n\n            # Prepare headers and body\n            headers = {\n                \'Content-type\': \'application/x-www-form-urlencoded\',\n                \'Accept\': \'text/plain\'\n            }\n            body = None\n            if data and method in [\'POST\', \'PUT\', \'DELETE\']:\n                body = urlencode(data)\n                headers[\'Content-Length\'] = str(len(body))\n\n            # Send the request\n            conn.request(method, path, body, headers)\n            response = conn.getresponse()\n\n            # Read and return the response\n            response_data = response.read()\n            conn.close()\n\n            return {\n                \'status\': response.status,\n                \'reason\': response.reason,\n                \'headers\': response.getheaders(),\n                \'body\': response_data.decode()\n            }\n        except Exception as e:\n            return {\'status\': \'error\', \'reason\': str(e)}\n```\n----- vulnerability_scanner.py\n```import re\n\nclass VulnerabilityScanner:\n    """\n    This class scans HTTP responses for potential vulnerabilities.\n    It is designed to identify common security issues such as SQL injection, XSS, and CSRF.\n    """\n\n    def scan_for_vulnerabilities(self, response: dict) -> list:\n        """\n        Scans the given HTTP response for vulnerabilities.\n\n        Args:\n            response (dict): The HTTP response dictionary containing status, headers, and body.\n\n        Returns:\n            list: A list of dictionaries, each representing a found vulnerability.\n        """\n        vulnerabilities = []\n        # Check for SQL Injection vulnerabilities\n        if self.detect_sql_injection(response[\'body\']):\n            vulnerabilities.append({\n                \'type\': \'SQL Injection\',\n                \'description\': \'SQL injection vulnerability detected.\',\n                \'payload\': response[\'body\']\n            })\n\n        # Check for XSS vulnerabilities\n        if self.detect_xss(response[\'body\']):\n            vulnerabilities.append({\n                \'type\': \'XSS\',\n                \'description\': \'Cross-site scripting vulnerability detected.\',\n                \'payload\': response[\'body\']\n            })\n\n        # Check for CSRF vulnerabilities\n        if self.detect_csrf(response[\'headers\']):\n            vulnerabilities.append({\n                \'type\': \'CSRF\',\n                \'description\': \'Cross-site request forgery vulnerability detected.\',\n                \'payload\': response[\'headers\']\n            })\n\n        return vulnerabilities\n\n    def detect_sql_injection(self, content: str) -> bool:\n        """\n        Detects potential SQL injection vectors in a given content string.\n\n        Args:\n            content (str): The content to scan for SQL injection patterns.\n\n        Returns:\n            bool: True if potential SQL injection patterns are found, False otherwise.\n        """\n        sql_injection_patterns = [r"\\\' OR \\d+=\\d+", r"admin\\\'--", r"DROP TABLE"]\n        return any(re.search(pattern, content) for pattern in sql_injection_patterns)\n\n    def detect_xss(self, content: str) -> bool:\n        """\n        Detects potential XSS (Cross-site Scripting) vectors in a given content string.\n\n        Args:\n            content (str): The content to scan for XSS patterns.\n\n        Returns:\n            bool: True if potential XSS patterns are found, False otherwise.\n        """\n        xss_patterns = [r"<script.*?>.*?</script>", r"javascript:", r"<iframe.*?>", r"onerror="]\n        return any(re.search(pattern, content, re.IGNORECASE) for pattern in xss_patterns)\n\n    def detect_csrf(self, headers: dict) -> bool:\n        """\n        Detects potential CSRF (Cross-site Request Forgery) vulnerabilities based on headers.\n\n        Args:\n            headers (dict): The HTTP headers to check for CSRF vulnerabilities.\n\n        Returns:\n            bool: True if headers lack CSRF protections, False otherwise.\n        """\n        # Check for common CSRF tokens in headers\n        csrf_tokens = [\'X-CSRF-Token\', \'CSRF-Token\', \'XSRF-TOKEN\', \'SameSite\']\n        return not any(token in headers for token in csrf_tokens)\n```\n----- exploit_engine.py\n```class ExploitEngine:\n    """\n    This class is responsible for exploiting identified vulnerabilities.\n    It interacts with the vulnerability scanner to receive vulnerabilities and attempts to exploit them.\n    """\n\n    def exploit_vulnerability(self, vulnerability: dict) -> dict:\n        """\n        Exploits a given vulnerability.\n\n        Args:\n            vulnerability (dict): A dictionary containing details about the vulnerability to be exploited.\n\n        Returns:\n            dict: A dictionary representing the results of the exploitation attempt.\n        """\n        exploit_result = {\n            \'vulnerability_type\': vulnerability[\'type\'],\n            \'exploited\': False,\n            \'details\': None\n        }\n\n        # Exploit logic based on the type of vulnerability\n        if vulnerability[\'type\'] == \'SQL Injection\':\n            exploit_result[\'exploited\'] = True\n            exploit_result[\'details\'] = \'Simulated SQL command to retrieve sensitive data.\'\n        elif vulnerability[\'type\'] == \'XSS\':\n            exploit_result[\'exploited\'] = True\n            exploit_result[\'details\'] = \'Simulated script execution on victim\\\'s browser.\'\n        elif vulnerability[\'type\'] == \'CSRF\':\n            exploit_result[\'exploited\'] = True\n            exploit_result[\'details\'] = \'Simulated forged request to perform actions on behalf of the user.\'\n\n        return exploit_result\n```\n\n\n## Code to be Reviewed: report_generator.py\n```Code\n## report_generator.py\n\nclass ReportGenerator:\n    """\n    This class generates reports based on the vulnerabilities found during the scanning and exploitation phases.\n    """\n\n    def generate_report(self, vulnerabilities: list) -> str:\n        """\n        Generates a textual report from a list of vulnerabilities.\n\n        Args:\n            vulnerabilities (list): A list of dictionaries, each representing a vulnerability.\n\n        Returns:\n            str: A formatted string report detailing all vulnerabilities.\n        """\n        if not vulnerabilities:\n            return "No vulnerabilities found."\n\n        report_lines = ["Vulnerability Report:"]\n        for vulnerability in vulnerabilities:\n            report_lines.append(f"Type: {vulnerability[\'type\']}")\n            report_lines.append(f"Description: {vulnerability[\'description\']}")\n            if \'exploited\' in vulnerability:\n                report_lines.append(f"Exploited: {\'Yes\' if vulnerability[\'exploited\'] else \'No\'}")\n                if vulnerability[\'exploited\']:\n                    report_lines.append(f"Details: {vulnerability[\'details\']}")\n            report_lines.append("")  # Add a blank line for better readability\n\n        return "\\n".join(report_lines)\n\n```\n\n\n\n# Format example 1\n## Code Review: report_generator.py\n1. urllib.parse import urlparse, urlencode\n\nclass HttpRequests:\n    """\n    This class handles HTTP interactions by sending requests to specified URLs.\n    It supports various HTTP methods like GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, and HEAD.\n    """\n    \n    def send_request(self, url: str, method: str = \'GET\', data: dict = None) -> dict:\n        """\n        Send an HTTP request to the specified URL with the given method and data.\n\n        Args:\n            url (str): The URL to which the request is sent.\n            method (str): The HTTP method to use (\'GET\', \'POST\', \'PUT\', etc.). Default is \'GET\'.\n            data (dict): The data to be sent in the request for methods like POST and PUT. Default is None.\n\n        Returns:\n            dict: A dictionary representing the response received from the server.\n        """\n        try:\n            # Parse the URL to extract components\n            parsed_url = urlparse(url)\n            host = parsed_url.netloc\n            path = parsed_url.path\n            if parsed_url.query:\n                path += \'?\' + parsed_url.query\n\n            # Create a connection based on the scheme\n            if parsed_url.scheme == "https":\n                conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection(host)\n            else:\n                conn = http.client.HTTPConnection(host)\n\n            # Prepare headers and body\n            headers = {\n                \'Content-type\': \'application/x-www-form-urlencoded\',\n                \'Accept\': \'text/plain\'\n            }\n            body = None\n            if data and method in [\'POST\', \'PUT\', \'DELETE\']:\n                body = urlencode(data)\n                headers[\'Content-Length\'] = str(len(body))\n\n            # Send the request\n            conn.request(method, path, body, headers)\n            response = conn.getresponse()\n\n            # Read and return the response\n            response_data = response.read()\n            conn.close()\n\n            return {\n                \'status\': response.status,\n                \'reason\': response.reason,\n                \'headers\': response.getheaders(),\n                \'body\': response_data.decode()\n            }\n        except Exception as e:\n            return {\'status\': \'error\', \'reason\': str(e)}\n```\n----- vulnerability_scanner.py\n```import re\n\nclass VulnerabilityScanner:\n    """\n    This class scans HTTP responses for potential vulnerabilities.\n    It is designed to identify common security issues such as SQL injection, XSS, and CSRF.\n    """\n\n    def scan_for_vulnerabilities(self, response: dict) -> list:\n        """\n        Scans the given HTTP response for vulnerabilities.\n\n        Args:\n            response (dict): The HTTP response dictionary containing status, headers, and body.\n\n        Returns:\n            list: A list of dictionaries, each representing a found vulnerability.\n        """\n        vulnerabilities = []\n        # Check for SQL Injection vulnerabilities\n        if self.detect_sql_injection(response[\'body\']):\n            vulnerabilities.append({\n                \'type\': \'SQL Injection\',\n                \'description\': \'SQL injection vulnerability detected.\',\n                \'payload\': response[\'body\']\n            })\n\n        # Check for XSS vulnerabilities\n        if self.detect_xss(response[\'body\']):\n            vulnerabilities.append({\n                \'type\': \'XSS\',\n                \'description\': \'Cross-site scripting vulnerability detected.\',\n                \'payload\': response[\'body\']\n            })\n\n        # Check for CSRF vulnerabilities\n        if self.detect_csrf(response[\'headers\']):\n            vulnerabilities.append({\n                \'type\': \'CSRF\',\n                \'description\': \'Cross-site request forgery vulnerability detected.\',\n                \'payload\': response[\'headers\']\n            })\n\n        return vulnerabilities\n\n    def detect_sql_injection(self, content: str) -> bool:\n        """\n        Detects potential SQL injection vectors in a given content string.\n\n        Args:\n            content (str): The content to scan for SQL injection patterns.\n\n        Returns:\n            bool: True if potential SQL injection patterns are found, False otherwise.\n        """\n        sql_injection_patterns = [r"\\\' OR \\d+=\\d+", r"admin\\\'--", r"DROP TABLE"]\n        return any(re.search(pattern, content) for pattern in sql_injection_patterns)\n\n    def detect_xss(self, content: str) -> bool:\n        """\n        Detects potential XSS (Cross-site Scripting) vectors in a given content string.\n\n        Args:\n            content (str): The content to scan for XSS patterns.\n\n        Returns:\n            bool: True if potential XSS patterns are found, False otherwise.\n        """\n        xss_patterns = [r"<script.*?>.*?</script>", r"javascript:", r"<iframe.*?>", r"onerror="]\n        return any(re.search(pattern, content, re.IGNORECASE) for pattern in xss_patterns)\n\n    def detect_csrf(self, headers: dict) -> bool:\n        """\n        Detects potential CSRF (Cross-site Request Forgery) vulnerabilities based on headers.\n\n        Args:\n            headers (dict): The HTTP headers to check for CSRF vulnerabilities.\n\n        Returns:\n            bool: True if headers lack CSRF protections, False otherwise.\n        """\n        # Check for common CSRF tokens in headers\n        csrf_tokens = [\'X-CSRF-Token\', \'CSRF-Token\', \'XSRF-TOKEN\', \'SameSite\']\n        return not any(token in headers for token in csrf_tokens)\n```\n----- exploit_engine.py\n```class ExploitEngine:\n    """\n    This class is responsible for exploiting identified vulnerabilities.\n    It interacts with the vulnerability scanner to receive vulnerabilities and attempts to exploit them.\n    """\n\n    def exploit_vulnerability(self, vulnerability: dict) -> dict:\n        """\n        Exploits a given vulnerability.\n\n        Args:\n            vulnerability (dict): A dictionary containing details about the vulnerability to be exploited.\n\n        Returns:\n            dict: A dictionary representing the results of the exploitation attempt.\n        """\n        exploit_result = {\n            \'vulnerability_type\': vulnerability[\'type\'],\n            \'exploited\': False,\n            \'details\': None\n        }\n\n        # Exploit logic based on the type of vulnerability\n        if vulnerability[\'type\'] == \'SQL Injection\':\n            exploit_result[\'exploited\'] = True\n            exploit_result[\'details\'] = \'Simulated SQL command to retrieve sensitive data.\'\n        elif vulnerability[\'type\'] == \'XSS\':\n            exploit_result[\'exploited\'] = True\n            exploit_result[\'details\'] = \'Simulated script execution on victim\\\'s browser.\'\n        elif vulnerability[\'type\'] == \'CSRF\':\n            exploit_result[\'exploited\'] = True\n            exploit_result[\'details\'] = \'Simulated forged request to perform actions on behalf of the user.\'\n\n        return exploit_result\n```\n----- report_generator.py\n```## report_generator.py\n\nclass ReportGenerator:\n    """\n    This class generates reports based on the vulnerabilities found during the scanning and exploitation phases.\n    """\n\n    def generate_report(self, vulnerabilities: list) -> str:\n        """\n        Generates a textual report from a list of vulnerabilities.\n\n        Args:\n            vulnerabilities (list): A list of dictionaries, each representing a vulnerability.\n\n        Returns:\n            str: A formatted string report detailing all vulnerabilities.\n        """\n        if not vulnerabilities:\n            return "No vulnerabilities found."\n\n        report_lines = ["Vulnerability Report:"]\n        for vulnerability in vulnerabilities:\n            report_lines.append(f"Type: {vulnerability[\'type\']}")\n            report_lines.append(f"Description: {vulnerability[\'description\']}")\n            if \'exploited\' in vulnerability:\n                report_lines.append(f"Exploited: {\'Yes\' if vulnerability[\'exploited\'] else \'No\'}")\n                if vulnerability[\'exploited\']:\n                    report_lines.append(f"Details: {vulnerability[\'details\']}")\n            report_lines.append("")  # Add a blank line for better readability\n\n        return "\\n".join(report_lines)\n```\n\n\n## Code to be Reviewed: main.py\n```Code\n## main.py\n\nfrom http_requests import HttpRequests\nfrom vulnerability_scanner import VulnerabilityScanner\nfrom exploit_engine import ExploitEngine\nfrom report_generator import ReportGenerator\n\nclass Main:\n    """\n    The Main class coordinates the flow between all modules, ensuring proper sequence of operations.\n    It integrates HttpRequests, VulnerabilityScanner, ExploitEngine, and ReportGenerator to perform\n    vulnerability scanning and exploitation.\n    """\n    def __init__(self):\n        """\n        Initializes the Main class with instances of all the necessary components.\n        """\n        self.http_requests = HttpRequests()\n        self.scanner = VulnerabilityScanner()\n        self.exploit_engine = ExploitEngine()\n        self.report_generator = ReportGenerator()\n\n    def run(self, url: str, method: str = \'GET\', data: dict = None):\n        """\n        The main entry point for running the vulnerability scanning and exploitation tool.\n\n        Args:\n            url (str): The URL to scan for vulnerabilities.\n            method (str): The HTTP method to use for the request.
